project.objective: A model-agnostic, LangGraph-pluggable agent SDK with orchestrator-spawned isolated subagents and an evidence-centric governance ledger. Stage 1 delivers the harness (Phases 0-8); Phase 0 is a single-agent loop end to end.

assumptions.text: PostgreSQL 16 is installed at C:/Program Files/PostgreSQL/16 and listening on localhost:5432, confirmed by an open socket. The superuser password is not yet known to this harness, so the Postgres connection string remains unresolved configuration.
Docker Desktop is installed (29.6.2) but its daemon is not running, so container-based Postgres is not an available fallback without starting Docker first.

<db_name> exists on localhost:5432, owned by <db_user>, PostgreSQL 16.13. Verified by DDL round trip: CREATE TABLE, insert with gen_random_uuid(), jsonb read, DROP TABLE all succeed; public schema was empty beforehand. gen_random_uuid() is built in on PG13+, so no pgcrypto extension is needed for UUID primary keys. This supersedes the earlier assumption that Postgres credentials were unresolved.

Two accepted M3 limitations, both reproduced by an independent reviewer and judged non-blocking. (1) _error_text catches only ValueError, so a 429 whose body is undecodable (verified with 6000-deep JSON) is classified ModelError rather than ModelRateLimited and is therefore NOT retried, deviating from FR-15. One-word fix, latent, needs a pathological body. (2) Redaction is asymmetric: a 4xx error body echoing the credential is redacted, but a 2xx body echoing it flows into message.content and reaches model context, contrary to NFR-4 read absolutely. Judged acceptable because error bodies routinely echo request context while success bodies do not, so the asymmetry tracks a real threat-model difference. Both should be closed when the file is next touched.

Declared M9 limitation A10, sharpened by the round 2 L4 reviewer: a model call billed inside send() with no usage reported is not counted in cost_usd. It is routine, not rare. RetryPolicy retries ModelTimeout by default, so when a provider processes a request but the client times out before reading the answer, the retry is a second billed call and the first is invisible to the loop. A 2xx whose body cannot be read or parsed is the same. Closing it needs the ModelClient contract to report attempts that received, or may have received, a response; recommended together with the native Anthropic adapter. Open.

invariants.text: Every ToolResult carries exactly one ContentProvenance. A tool result that reaches the model or the session store without provenance is a defect, not a default.
Every persisted row in every table carries non-null tenant_id and project_id. Multi-tenancy is enforced at write time, never assumed at read time.

ToolExecutor's order is fixed: resolve, then validate arguments, then permission check, then execute. A tool whose arguments failed validation must never reach the permission check, and a denied tool must never reach execution.
MODEL_API_KEY never enters model context, never enters a persisted row, and never appears in a RunEvent payload. Credentials reach the provider adapter only.
Application code calls Runner.run() and nothing else. If a test or example imports AgentLoop, ToolExecutor or any other internal collaborator directly, the public API boundary has already leaked.

Only AgentSDKError subclasses may escape ModelClient.send(). A provider's JSONDecodeError, AttributeError or httpx.StreamError reaching AgentLoop is a defect: the loop cannot classify what it cannot name. Note httpx.StreamError descends from RuntimeError, not HTTPError, so catching HTTPError alone is insufficient.

A boundary's error path must not be able to raise. send() wraps any non-AgentSDKError, but str(exc) runs inside that handler: a hostile __str__ that raises, or returns a non-string, escapes the very mechanism built to make the boundary total. Rendering a caught exception goes through _describe_failure, which guards str(exc) explicitly and sits inside a last-resort catch returning a fixed string.

Runner.run() is a total boundary: it always returns a RunResult with a terminal status and never lets an exception reach application code. ToolExecutor.execute() is likewise total and always returns an outcome. Configuration errors (unknown model client, invalid RunConfig) are the deliberate exception and raise at the call site, because a caller bug must surface loudly rather than hide in a RunResult nobody inspects. BaseException passes through as control flow.

Any number that arrives from a model provider, a persisted event payload or a replayed run reaches a typed field only through a total coercion that cannot raise on Exception. Concretely: never call int(), float() or similar directly on such a value; construct the dataclass and let it coerce. Violations have been rejected three times.

Amends INVARIANT-af776957 (M12, FR-50, 2026-09-15). Runner.run() is a total boundary: it returns a RunResult with a terminal status and lets no Exception reach application code, and ToolExecutor.execute() is likewise total. Configuration errors raise at the call site before any run starts, from Runner.run and Runner.start alike. Cancellation is recorded, then re-raised: cancelling the task that awaits Runner.run, or a CancelledError raised by a collaborator, ends the run with status cancelled, RunCancelled as its last event and its usage and cost recorded, and CancelledError then reaches the caller; RunHandle.result() returns that cancelled RunResult. Any other BaseException passes through as control flow.
invariants.source: M12 FR-50, approved in L4 review round 1, 2026-09-15

decisions.title: ADR-13 resolved: OpenAI-compatible wire format
decisions.text: The bring-your-own endpoint is a LiteLLM proxy at the PwC GenAI shared service. Probed directly: POST /v1/chat/completions returns OpenAI-shaped responses with tool_calls, finish_reason and usage; the error envelope carries LiteLLM provider_specific_fields. Phase 0 therefore implements an OpenAI-compatible ModelClient first, not a Bedrock-native one.

decisions.title: Phase 0 is the entire spec scope
decisions.text: This specification covers only the Phase 0 single-agent skeleton, which the LLD already details to implementable precision. Phases 2-8 get their own Genesis specification when each starts, per the design docs' explicit refusal to write low-level design for components that do not exist yet.

decisions.title: ADR-27 kept: PrincipalContext as lean metadata
decisions.text: PrincipalContext stays in Phase 0 as a nullable JSONB column on runs plus an unread field on RunConfig. Confirmed by the human despite the design docs flagging it as the most speculative Phase 0 addition; rationale is that retrofitting an identity concept through PermissionChecker later is expensive while an unread column is nearly free.

decisions.title: System instructions ride on ModelRequest.instructions, not a fourth Role
decisions.text: The LLD fixes the messages.role column enum at user/assistant/tool. Adding Role.SYSTEM to carry an AgentSpec's instructions would either desynchronise the enum from the persisted schema or force a schema change. Instead ModelRequest gains an 'instructions' field and each provider adapter renders it in its own idiom (the OpenAI-compatible adapter emits a leading system message). Keeps the persisted enum honest and keeps system-prompt handling a provider concern.

decisions.title: Secrets are wrapped in a Secret type, not protected by __repr__ alone
decisions.text: L4 review demonstrated that overriding Settings.__repr__ leaves dataclasses.asdict, astuple and vars leaking the raw credential, and asdict is the idiom that will write FR-11's ExecutionManifest row. Redaction now lives on the value: config.Secret refuses to render under repr, str, format, asdict, astuple and vars, and the raw value is reachable only through an explicit .reveal() that greps cleanly. The adapter additionally redacts the key from any provider error body copied into a ModelError message, because those messages land in FR-10's persisted RunFailed payload.

decisions.title: The ModelClient boundary is total, not an enumeration of known exceptions
decisions.text: Three review rounds each found exactly one more exception type escaping send(): JSONDecodeError, then TypeError from an unhashable dict key, then OverflowError from int(float('inf')). Each was fixed by adding one more guard inside _parse. That approach does not converge, because no enumeration of failure modes is complete. send() now delegates to _send and re-raises AgentSDKError untouched while wrapping any other Exception as ModelError, chaining the cause and redacting the message. BaseException (CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit) deliberately passes through as control flow. Specific guards remain because a precise diagnosis beats a generic one, but correctness of the invariant no longer depends on their completeness. Cost accepted: a genuine adapter bug now surfaces as ModelError with the original type named in the message.

decisions.title: Retry belongs to the ModelClient and to exactly one layer
decisions.text: AgentLoop retried transient model errors as a backstop while the adapter retried too. Neither knew about the other and both were on by default, so a single timeout became 3 x 3 = 9 HTTP calls where FR-15 permits 3. Independently measured at 9 by an L4 reviewer through the public API. The loop's retry is deleted: retry lives where ModelTimeout and ModelRateLimited are classified, which is the adapter, and a client that declines to retry is making a policy decision the loop must not silently override. Verified back to exactly 3 attempts.

decisions.title: tool_profile gates execution, not visibility, in Phase 0
decisions.text: An L4 reviewer found AgentSpec.tool_profile self-contradictory: the comment said an empty profile meant every registered tool while the code denied all, and the model was offered every registered schema regardless of profile (profile ('echo',) still advertised rm_rf and send_email). Resolved: an empty profile permits NOTHING, because an allowlist that opens the gates when empty fails silently open. The comment is corrected to match. Visibility filtering is deliberately NOT added in Phase 0: deciding what an agent may SEE is ContextPolicy's job in Phase 2, and leaving every schema visible keeps AC-2's permission-denial path reachable in the golden eval. Revisit when ContextPolicy lands.

decisions.title: Manifest is an argument to start_run, not a second write
decisions.text: PostgresRunStore.start_run takes the execution manifest as a required argument and writes both rows in one transaction. Over two connections, AC-6 (exactly one manifest per run) held only when nothing failed in between: a transient error committed a runs row with no manifest and no RunStarted event, since that emit follows both writes. RunRecorder deliberately omits write_manifest so no backend can offer the Runner a way to start a run without one. Found by the M5 round-1 independent review.

decisions.title: Provider-supplied numbers are coerced by the type, not by call sites
decisions.text: Usage coerces every field in __post_init__ through one total helper, agentsdk.model.token_count. The adapter's _as_int is deleted rather than duplicated, so there is one implementation. Rationale: the same defect was rejected three times in three milestones at three call sites -- M3 round 3 (int(float('inf')) -> OverflowError in the adapter), and M5 round 2 (the same shape in _usage_from_events, on the total boundary's ERROR path where raising is worst). Each was fixed where found, which guaranteed the next unguarded int() would be a fresh defect rather than a caught regression. token_count is total over Exception but NOT over BaseException, so KeyboardInterrupt remains control flow. A nonsense count degrades to 0: token accounting is never worth failing a run over. Generalises the M3 total-boundary lesson from exception handling to value coercion -- enumerate nothing, make the bad state unrepresentable at the type.

decisions.title: Canonical primitives are storable by construction
decisions.text: ToolCall, Message and the ToolExecutor reject values no durable store can hold, using one total helper (primitives.unstorable_reason). Unstorable tool arguments are cleared and routed onto arguments_error, the channel undecodable JSON already uses; unstorable Message.content raises, because content has no error channel and dropping the byte would edit the record NFR-3 calls authoritative; an unstorable tool RESULT becomes an ordinary tool error so the run continues. Rationale: json.loads is RFC-8259-correct and turns 1e400 into inf and a U+0000 escape into a NUL; JSONB holds neither, so the same run completed in memory and failed against Postgres, breaking postgres.py's stated contract that the loop cannot tell which store it is talking to. The check is in the primitives rather than in the OpenAI adapter because NFR-1 claims a new provider is a configuration change -- verified with a custom ModelClient, not just the adapter where it was found. Third consecutive round where the durable fix was upstream of where the symptom appeared.

decisions.title: Message tenancy is derived from the run row, never from the caller
decisions.text: PostgresSessionStore.append takes tenant_id and project_id from the runs row in the INSERT ... SELECT itself, and matches the caller's RunScope in the WHERE so a mismatch errors rather than being quietly corrected. A rowcount of 0 means the run does not exist or belongs to another tenant, and raises. Rationale: messages.tenant_id is denormalised so isolation needs no join, which is only worth having if the copy cannot disagree with the original; previously a caller could file messages under a tenant the run did not belong to. Re-measured concurrency after the change: safety unchanged (0 duplicates, contiguous), availability improved (0-1 of 12 writers lose, previously 4 of 12) -- the Phase 2 availability item still stands.

decisions.title: Storability is applied by walking every field, not a list of names
decisions.text: Primitive constructors call _replace_unstorable_text, which walks dataclasses.fields() and replaces any unstorable string field with the marker '<unstorable>', recording the reason on the type's existing error channel where one exists. Applied by ToolCall, ToolResult, ContentProvenance, Message and ModelResponse. Rationale: five review rounds found the storability CHECK correct but its APPLICATION an enumeration -- Message.content, ToolCall.arguments and ToolResult.content were guarded while id, name, tool_call_id, source_uri_or_hash and provider_response_id reached the same columns unguarded. Walking the fields means a field added later is covered without anyone remembering. Identifiers are replaced rather than refused so a NUL in a tool name becomes an ordinary ToolNotFound error result -- what happens without persistence -- instead of a run that dies at the write with no record of what the model said (NFR-3).

decisions.title: history() is tenant-scoped on read, not only on write
decisions.text: PostgresSessionStore.history requires a bound RunScope and filters on tenant_id and project_id, like append. Previously a store bound to tenant B could read tenant A's messages given only a run id. The counter-argument is real -- FR-9's signature is history(run_id) and run ids are UUIDv4 -- but NFR-2's premise is that tenancy is ENFORCED, not that identifiers are unguessable, and an id is a capability only until one leaks into a log or a support ticket. The cost is one WHERE clause against an index that already exists. Raised as 'worth a decision, not a fix' by the M5 round-5 reviewer; recorded here rather than left implicit.

decisions.title: Tenancy is enforced on every runs and trace statement
decisions.text: PostgresRunStore.finish_run and get_run take a RunScope, and PostgresTrace.reconstruct takes one too; all filter on tenant_id and project_id. Extends DECISION-e692386f from history() to the rest. Rationale: AC-7's own vehicle was deciding the tenancy question the opposite way to the session store one function over, and the same question answered inconsistently is worse than either answer applied consistently. RunScope itself now refuses an unstorable run_id, tenant_id or project_id, and start_run refuses an unstorable agent_spec_id or model_id: these are caller-supplied configuration rather than model output, so there is no run to keep alive and refusing beats degrading -- the error names the field instead of surfacing as an opaque psycopg failure later.

decisions.title: Configuration refuses by name; model output is replaced and flagged
decisions.text: primitives.refuse_unstorable_fields walks dataclasses.fields() and RAISES with the field named; used by RunScope and PrincipalContext. primitives._replace_unstorable_text walks the same fields but REPLACES with a marker and records the reason; used by ToolCall, ToolResult, ContentProvenance, Message and ModelResponse. The split is deliberate: model output has a run in flight that should survive a bad byte, whereas configuration is supplied before anything starts, so there is nothing to preserve and a named error beats an opaque psycopg failure several frames later. refuse_unstorable_fields also covers fields of ANY shape, not just str -- unstorable_reason recurses -- because round 7 found PrincipalContext.scopes, a tuple[str, ...] whose contents reached JSONB unchecked while the str-only replacement walk saw nothing.

decisions.title: Storability checks are keyed by the destination column's type
decisions.text: postgres.column_rejection_reason(value, sql_type) replaces bare unstorable_reason at the write sites: it keeps the serialisability answer for TEXT and JSONB and adds the int32 range for INTEGER. Rationale: 'can this be serialised' and 'does this fit this column' are different questions, and conflating them was M5 round 8's defect. RunConfig also bounds max_turns above, so the run fails identically with and without persistence -- the divergence was the defect, not the error type. Related: ToolSpec now refuses an input_schema that cannot be serialised at construction, because schema_hash() is reached only through build_manifest and therefore only when persistence is configured, which turned a developer error into a database-dependent failure of an unrelated run.

decisions.title: Schema tests assert constraint DEFINITIONS and column types
decisions.text: test_schema_sql_itself_declares_the_constraints now reads pg_get_constraintdef and information_schema column types in the throwaway namespace, asserting UNIQUE (run_id, sequence_no), PRIMARY KEY (run_id) and runs.max_turns being INTEGER, rather than asserting that a constraint of some type exists. Rationale: rewriting UNIQUE (run_id, sequence_no) to (run_id, message_id) previously left the suite green -- the same coverage-not-fitness shape as M5 round 8, this time in the schema tests. It matters more than a normal blind spot because schema.sql has no migration path and IS the deployment artefact, so damage stays invisible until the next fresh database; and because round 8's int32 range check is justified entirely by max_turns being INTEGER, which nothing asserted.

decisions.title: One psycopg_pool per DSN, validated on checkout, with no retry on a write that fails mid-flight
decisions.text: FR-20. Store methods share one psycopg_pool ConnectionPool per DSN (psycopg_pool 3.2.6, maintained by the psycopg project; NFR-6 bars vendor agent SDKs, not infrastructure libraries). Built with check=ConnectionPool.check_connection: without it the pool handed out connections the server had already closed, so a Postgres restart, failover or idle kill failed a whole batch of runs (M7 round 2: five killed, 3 of 8 runs completed), a regression against the per-call connect it replaced. A connection that dies during a write still fails that write, deliberately: the insert may have committed before the reply was lost, and retrying a MAX + 1 append would duplicate the message rather than recover it. SPEC.md named this dependency a decision to record; round 1 found it unrecorded.

decisions.title: Concurrent appends to one run queue on an advisory lock instead of retrying
decisions.text: FR-19. Both sequenced write paths take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(run_id), space), with separate spaces for messages and events. A bounded retry lets exactly one writer through per round of contention, so N simultaneous writers need N rounds and any cap small enough to be safe is too small to help. The lock is transaction-scoped: released on commit, on rollback, and if the process dies. hashtext collisions only serialise unrelated runs briefly (verified by the round-2 reviewer with a real collision across 3 processes and 12 threads, 72 of 72 commits). The UNIQUE (run_id, sequence_no) constraint stays as the invariant at rest.

decisions.title: Store I/O runs on worker threads; SessionStore and EventSink stay synchronous
decisions.text: FR-20. Every store call made during a run goes through asyncio.to_thread, and ToolExecutor awaits whatever its emit callback returns so the Runner can offload ToolCalled too. Making the protocols async would replace a contract NFR-7 says to extend and rewrite 94 call sites across the approved suites. The M7 round-1 reviewer accepted this reading of non-blocking I/O. Enforced by a test that records the thread of every pool connection checkout across five run paths, including every kind of tool failure; pinned by a test that postgres.py opens no connection outside the pool.

decisions.title: Migrations: schema.sql is baseline 0001, everything under one lock, one transaction each, checksummed
decisions.text: FR-17. apply_schema runs schema.sql and then numbered migrations inside a single session-level advisory lock, so workers initialising an empty database serialise instead of racing (before this, 1 of 8 succeeded). Each migration commits in its own transaction with its bookkeeping row, so a failure keeps earlier migrations applied. Applied migrations carry a SHA-256 of their newline-normalised text, because line endings in this repository are mixed; an edited applied migration is refused by name, and rows applied before checksums existed are trusted on first sight and recorded. Persistence.postgres() does this as blocking DDL on the calling thread; build it once at process start, or pass create_schema=False.

decisions.title: parent_run_id accepts a canonical UUID string or a uuid.UUID, nothing else
decisions.text: FR-21. The guard accepts only the canonical string form, because uuid.UUID() is more permissive than a Postgres uuid column (it strips a urn:uuid: prefix the column refuses), and accepts uuid.UUID objects outright, because that is the type get_run and PostgresTrace return for run ids. RunConfig normalises to the canonical string. Refusing uppercase, braced and unhyphenated strings the column would accept is deliberate: every run id the SDK issues is canonical.

decisions.title: A response cut off by the output-token limit ends the run as failed, reason max_tokens
decisions.text: Owner decision, 2026-09-12. When a model response stops because it reached the output-token limit, the run ends with status failed and reason max_tokens. Chosen over adding a new run status and over keeping the run completed. Planning only, not implemented: today the loop decides on tool-call presence, so a truncated response with no tool calls currently ends as completed. It changes the terminal status of an existing path, so it needs a requirement and a test before it lands.

decisions.title: ADR-06 stays Proposed until Phase 2 budget work
decisions.text: Owner decision, 2026-09-12. ADR-06 (hard run ceiling, per-child reservation, reclaim of unused budget) remains Proposed. It must be decided before the budget work in Phase 2, and is not a precondition for M9 or M10.
decisions.source: Owner roadmap review against the Claude Agent SDK and the OpenAI Agents SDK, 2026-09-12

decisions.title: ADR-06 Accepted: run ceiling, per-child reservation and reclaim, enforced softly in USD and tokens
decisions.text: Owner decision, 2026-09-12. Supersedes DECISION-f39da722, which kept ADR-06 Proposed. (1) Model: run ceiling plus per-child reservation plus reclaim of unused budget. Inherited/split and a flat cap are rejected; a flat cap would contradict ADR-10. The word hard is dropped from the name because enforcement is soft. (2) Units: USD and tokens. A run may set a USD ceiling, a token ceiling, or both, and whichever is reached first applies. Reservations and reclaim track every unit that has a ceiling. A USD ceiling on a model with no price is a configuration error raised at the call site; a token ceiling always applies. (3) Enforcement: soft. Spend is checked before each model call, and an agent already at or over its reservation makes no further call, so an agent can exceed its reservation by at most one model call and a run can exceed its ceiling by at most one call per concurrently running agent, orchestrator included; SchedulerLimits.max_concurrent_subagents bounds that overshoot. Overshoot is charged to the run, and once run spend reaches its ceiling no new model call or child run starts. (4) At the limit: a child that reaches its reservation ends failed with reason budget_exceeded, and so does a run that reaches its ceiling. Extra allocation comes only from a deterministic orchestrator policy drawing on the unallocated reserve, never at the request of the model. (5) Sizing: the planner model proposes each PlanNode budget_reservation and a fixed policy rule caps it. Left to the Phase 2 specification: the cap rule itself, the fallback when the planner proposes nothing, and the sizes of the orchestrator reserve and the unallocated reserve. (6) Scope: a nested child reserves from the reservation of its parent, never directly from the run pool. Retries of a node draw on that node reservation, and replanning stays inside the run ceiling. Budgets for plain single-agent runs are not part of this decision. Budgets across a tenant or across runs remain deferred per ADR-10.

decisions.title: M9 D1: content_filter also ends a run as failed
decisions.text: Owner approved 2026-09-12. A model response whose stop reason is content_filter ends the run failed with error content_filter, under the same rules as max_tokens: the message is recorded and no tool call from it executes. An unrecognised stop reason keeps its current behaviour. SPEC FR-26, AC-20.

decisions.title: M9 D2: reasoning effort requires an explicit output limit
decisions.text: Setting reasoning_effort with no explicit max_output_tokens on the agent or the run is a configuration error raised at the Runner.run call site, because with the adapter default of 1024 Claude Haiku over the gateway returns HTTP 400 (max_tokens must exceed the thinking budget). SPEC FR-28, AC-21.

decisions.title: M9 D3: ModelPricing replaces cost_per_token
decisions.text: ModelCapabilities.cost_per_token, read by nothing in agentsdk, tests or scripts, is replaced by ModelPricing with input, output, cache read and cache write prices, and FR-12 is amended. Cost is a Decimal and None when unknown, never 0. SPEC FR-12, FR-30.

decisions.title: M9 D4: persist token totals and the prices used
decisions.text: Migration 0003 adds the six token totals and cost_usd to runs, and max_output_tokens, reasoning_effort and the pricing used to execution_manifests, so a stored cost can be checked after prices change. SPEC FR-31, AC-24.

decisions.title: M10 D5: every tool output is capped at 50000 characters by default
decisions.text: ToolSpec.max_output_chars defaults to 50000 with no uncapped setting, and applies to every ToolResult the executor returns, including errors and after_tool substitutions. SPEC FR-41, AC-33.

decisions.title: M10 D6: literal grep and refusal of multiply linked files
decisions.text: grep matches literal text only, because a model supplied regex can backtrack catastrophically and a timeout cannot interrupt a synchronous function. A file with more than one hard link is refused, because a hard link to an outside file cannot be told apart by its path. SPEC FR-36, FR-37.

decisions.title: M10 D7: symlink escape cases run on this host with Developer Mode
decisions.text: AC-28 creates real symlinks and those cases fail rather than skip. This host refuses symlink creation without Windows Developer Mode (WinError 1314), so the owner turns Developer Mode on before the M10 gate runs. SPEC AC-28 and Constraints.

decisions.title: M10 D8: M10 is high risk
decisions.text: M10 is a security surface (filesystem confinement, SSRF, credential isolation) and enters the plan with risk high. M9 stays medium.

decisions.title: M9 and M10 D9: examples 09 and 10 are the demo commands
decisions.text: scripts/09_limits_and_cost.py and scripts/10_builtin_tools.py, run offline, are the demo commands for M9 and M10. AC-17 covers both, and the README and scripts/README.md list them, so the eight examples wording changes. SPEC FR-34, FR-42.

decisions.title: M9 and M10 D10: task add may regenerate PLAN.md
decisions.text: The owner authorised Genesis to regenerate .genesis/PLAN.md when the M9 and M10 tasks are added. This covers that regeneration only: DONE.html, and any manual edit of PLAN.md, still need asking first.

decisions.title: M9 and M10 D10 extended: PLAN.md regeneration for the whole setup sequence
decisions.text: The owner extended D10 on 2026-09-12: Genesis may regenerate .genesis/PLAN.md for the whole M9 setup sequence, which is spec approve, task add for M9 and M10, plan check and plan approve. spec check had already regenerated it once before this permission, changing only the phase and plan approval lines, and that was disclosed to the owner.

decisions.title: Uncounted billed calls are closed with the native Anthropic adapter, not in M10
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-12 on ASSUMPTION-b7463ca2. A model call billed inside send() with no usage reported is routine under the default retry of timeouts: a provider processes the request, the client times out, and the retry is a second billed call the loop never sees; a 2xx whose body cannot be read is the same. It is closed by extending the ModelClient contract so a client reports every attempt that received, or may have received, a response, and the run accounts for such an attempt, at minimum by reporting its cost as unknown rather than omitting it. The change lands with the native Anthropic Messages adapter in Phase 0/1, where the contract is being extended anyway. It is not part of M10. Until then the limitation stays declared.

decisions.title: M10 D11: file tools are Windows-only in this release
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13. The file tools confine paths with Windows handle APIs: CreateFileW with backup semantics, GetFinalPathNameByHandleW on the opened handle, and directory enumeration through that same handle. This host cannot test a POSIX implementation, so on any other platform constructing a file tool raises NotImplementedError rather than shipping untested confinement code. Declared as a limitation in the README, the scripts README, example 10 and the M10 review prompt. A POSIX implementation is future work with its own tests.

decisions.title: M10 D12: an error after a tool ran carries its full declared provenance
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13, refining FR-40. When a tool that declares provenance has run and then fails (it raised, timed out, returned unstorable content, or a hook failed after it ran), the error result carries the declared origin as well as the declared trust zone, instruction authority and taint flags, and source_uri_or_hash stays the executor error URN. FR-40 named only trust zone, authority and taint. Origin follows the existing executor rule that origin names where the call was directed. Failures before the tool ran keep executor_error provenance.

decisions.title: A bounded executor for file tools is a Phase 2 prerequisite
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13 on M10 review caveat C2. The file tools keep the shared default thread pool in M10. Before Phase 2 makes concurrent tool calls routine, the file tools get their own bounded executor or semaphore, with a test that store latency stays flat while the file tool pool is saturated.

decisions.title: M10 D13: in-process forgery of objects is outside the threat model
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13, after M10 review rounds 3 and 4 were rejected on the same seam. Tools, hooks, permission checkers, registries and other in-process caller code are trusted code. A defect that requires such code to forge objects past their constructors or the language machinery (object.__setattr__ on a frozen dataclass, __new__ without __init__, str.__new__ on a str Enum, __class__ assignment, attribute access overrides, ctypes) is outside the M10 threat model. The checks that exist stay as defence in depth, and such a finding is recorded as a caveat, not a blocker. In scope remain everything a model, a remote server or a file on disk can supply, and caller code that uses the public types as documented. The round 4 finding, a str.__new__ forged enum label, is closed anyway with an identity check against the real members, because the fix is small and the label is on the persisted path.

decisions.title: Phase 2 D1: the Phase 2 specification is written in two increments
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13. The first increment specifies in full requirements M11 concurrency foundations (a bounded executor for file tools, SchedulerLimits, parallel read-only tool calls, the M10 carry-overs), M12 RunHandle with runtime event streaming and cancellation, and M13 ArtifactRef and ArtifactStore. The Orchestrator, PlanVersion DAG, PlanNode acceptance criteria, the ADR-06 budget governor, ContextPolicy and replanning are outlined with their open decisions and specified in a second increment once M11 to M13 exist, following the design rule of not specifying components before the ones they depend on exist.

decisions.title: Phase 2 D2: read-only tool calls in one turn run in parallel by default, bounded
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13, refining DECISION-e6228dd4. When a model response carries several tool calls, the calls whose tools declare read_only True run concurrently by default, capped by SchedulerLimits defaults and any per-tool limits; every other call runs sequentially. Tool results are appended to history in the order the model issued the calls, whatever order they finish in, so history stays deterministic.

decisions.title: Phase 2 D3: a cancelled run ends with a new terminal status cancelled
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13. RunHandle.cancel() ends a run with a new terminal RunStatus.CANCELLED, persisted through a migration and announced by a RunCancelled event, with usage and cost recorded as on every other terminal path. Reusing failed with reason cancelled was rejected because a cancelled run could then not be told apart from a failure without parsing the error.

decisions.title: Phase 2 D4: Phase 2 work happens on a phase-2 branch
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-13. main was fast-forwarded to the M10 commit aa146f3 with no merge commit and nothing pushed, and Phase 2 specification and milestone work continues on the branch phase-2.

decisions.title: Phase 2 increment 1 decisions P2-D5 to P2-D11 accepted
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14. Accepted as proposed in SPEC.md: P2-D5 a default of 4 concurrent tool calls per run with no per-tool or per-provider limit unless set; P2-D6 one SDK-owned file-tool thread pool of 4 threads; P2-D7 a run cancelled with a model call in flight reports cost None; P2-D8 artifacts in Postgres with content capped at 10485760 bytes; P2-D9 ToolCalled events of a batch emitted as each call finishes, their order among themselves unspecified; P2-D10 migrations 0004 scheduler limits, 0005 cancelled status, 0006 artifacts; P2-D11 examples 11, 12 and 13.

decisions.title: P2-D14: parallel tool calls are opt-in per tool through ToolSpec.concurrency_safe
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 after the M11 spec review. A tool call joins a parallel batch only when its tool declares concurrency_safe True, a new ToolSpec field defaulting to False that enters schema_hash only when True; the built-in read-only tools declare it. ToolSpec.read_only defaults to True, so keying batches on it would have made every undeclared tool parallel, including the golden eval tool that deletes records. SPEC FR-44, AC-35.

decisions.title: M14: per-call timings and a minimal OpenTelemetry exporter, pulled forward from Phase 8
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 on backlog I-18. Phase 2 increment 1 gains M14: model, tool and terminal events record timings, and agentsdk.telemetry exports a run as invoke_agent, chat and execute_tool spans following OpenTelemetry semantic conventions v1.40.0, exporting no content and a cost only when it is known, through an optional otel extra pinned at 1.44.0 (P2-D12). The full mapping stays in Phase 8 (ADR-22). SPEC FR-57 to FR-60.

decisions.title: M15: the first ADR-12 comparison runs before the Phase 2 increment 2 spec
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 on backlog I-16. ADR-12 had never run. M15 compares this SDK with the raw Claude Agent SDK on 12 file tasks, 3 runs each, both with bedrock.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5 through the same gateway, read-only tools on both sides, costed from one ModelPricing; web tasks are left out, and claude-agent-sdk 0.2.152 is only an eval dependency (P2-D13). A pre-flight must show the Claude Agent SDK works against the gateway, or M15 stops for an owner decision. SPEC FR-61 to FR-63.

decisions.title: General agent: option B, a general-agent preset in a new Phase 5A
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 on the general agent question (local note docs/07, backlog I-15). The SDK stays a framework and adds, in a new Phase 5A after Phase 5, a default general AgentSpec preset with tuned instructions, a general-purpose subagent, and a model-driven autonomous mode alongside the DAG, all inside budgets, sandbox and permissions. Phases 6 to 8 keep their numbers. This reopens the scope of ADR-02 for Phase 5A.

decisions.title: Context compaction moves from Phase 7 to Phase 2 increment 2
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 on backlog I-17 and I-24. ContextCompactor is specified with Phase 2 increment 2, beside ContextPolicy, instead of Phase 7, so long subagent runs and later screenshot-heavy runs have it in time. Phase 7 keeps its number with no scope of its own.

decisions.title: Every ideas-backlog item placed in the roadmap register before Phase 2
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14. Each item of the local ideas backlog (docs/06, I-01 to I-24) has a landing point in the deferred-capabilities register of agent-sdk-project-master.md section 5 and agent-sdk-master-design-v0.3.md section 9, and the questions a later spec must decide (bounded loop nodes, prompt-cache staggering, child-output scanning, a pricing source, tool visibility) are listed in the SPEC.md increment 2 outline. Open questions stay open until their phase spec decides them.

decisions.title: A1: NFR-15 amended for batch ordering under max_concurrent_tools 1
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 on author issue A1 of the M11 review. NFR-15 said a run with max_concurrent_tools 1 produces the same events as before Phase 2, while FR-44 and AC-35 pass every call of a batch of concurrency_safe calls through steps 1 to 5 before the first executes, and AC-45 (M14) depends on that queueing. So under max_concurrent_tools 1, before_tool sees every call of such a batch first, and a call refused at steps 1 to 5 records its ToolCalled before the events of calls issued ahead of it; history and the results the model receives keep issue order, and tools that do not declare concurrency_safe are unchanged. NFR-15 now names this ordering as an exception. The code is unchanged.

decisions.title: The development database password printed by an M10 probe is not rotated
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14. An M10 verification probe printed the password of the local development Postgres on 2026-09-13. The database is for development only and is not going to production, so the owner declined rotation for now. Probes must still never print a password or a connection string. Revisit if the database becomes reachable from other machines, the password is used anywhere else, or the database moves toward shared or production use. Measured 2026-09-14: Postgres listens on all interfaces on port 5432, and no enabled inbound Windows Firewall allow rule names it. The SPEC.md Risks entry is updated to match.

decisions.title: GitHub receives a filtered copy of the history; the local repository keeps the full record
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14. A scan of all 52 commits found no credential, token or private key, but found local Windows paths with the username, one account email, and the database user and name. GitHub siva-rgb/Custom-Agent now receives a copy of main and phase-2 in which every file version and commit message has those values replaced with placeholders (owner, <repo>, <user>, owner account, <db_user>, <db_name>); the local repository is never rewritten. The copy is built by git-filter-repo 2.47.0 from scripts under .git/publish-filter, which git never pushes, and a verifier refuses to publish if any listed value or any .env credential value is left in history, if any file outside .genesis and SPEC.md changed, or if an author, committer or date changed. Verified to fail on the unfiltered history (7 problems) and to produce identical commit ids on two builds, so later pushes fast-forward. The commit author siva-rgb keeps the existing email by owner choice. Pushed 2026-09-14: main force-updated with lease from cc2f0d6 to 51e48e7, and phase-2 created at d3d819d. GitHub may keep the replaced commits reachable by direct link for a while. Direct pushes from the local repository are disabled through the origin pushurl.

decisions.title: M12: a tool that ignores cancellation is a declared limitation; cancellation stays cooperative
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-14 at the M12 pre-flight, on the caveat of the M11 round 2 review. A tool that catches CancelledError and carries on cannot be stopped. Cancellation stays cooperative: RunHandle.cancel() cancels every running tool call and waits until each one actually stops, so such a tool delays the end of the run for as long as it runs, and the run ends cancelled only when that tool returns or raises. No grace period and no setting are added, and FR-44 keeps its rule that a cancelled batch leaves no call running. Recorded in SPEC.md Risks beside the existing risk that a running file tool cannot be interrupted; stopping arbitrary code belongs to the Phase 5 sandbox.

decisions.title: FR-56 amended: EXPECTED_EXAMPLES gains 09 to 12 in M13, and 13 with M14
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-15 before the M13 pre-flight. FR-56 said the distribution test EXPECTED_EXAMPLES gains 09 to 13 in M13, but scripts/13_telemetry.py is the M14 example (P2-D11, FR-60), so naming it in M13 would fail AC-17 until M14. M13 adds 09 to 12 (09 and 10 already exist and run without being named; 11 and 12 are the M13 examples), and M14 adds 13 with its example. No scope moves between milestones.

decisions.title: M14: live example 13 sends its spans to a local Jaeger container
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-15 at the M14 readiness check. The live mode of scripts/13_telemetry.py (FR-60) sends its spans over OTLP/HTTP to a local Jaeger container run in Docker, with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318 set in .env and named in .env.example, and the Jaeger UI on localhost:16686; the image and its version are pinned when the live run is prepared. The owner starts Docker Desktop, whose daemon was not running at the check (ASSUMPTION-53240ce4). The M14 tests need no collector: AC-47 points an exporter at a closed port. Also decided: the SPEC.md decision-table heading is corrected to show P2-D12 accepted on 2026-09-14 (DECISION-8793bdd7), with P2-D13 still proposed.

decisions.title: M14: parent_run_id is recorded in RunStarted and a declared provider name in ModelCalled
decisions.text: Owner decisions 2026-09-15 at the M14 pre-flight, closing two gaps found against the code. FR-58 and FR-59 need a run parent_run_id and a declared provider name, but the exporter consumes only a RunHandle or a RunResult; no event payload, RunResult or RunHandle carries parent_run_id (it lives in RunConfig and the runs row only), and no model client declares a provider name. (1) RunStarted gains parent_run_id, None for a top-level run, listed in FR-57 so that NFR-15 covers it; the exporter reads a run parent from its own RunStarted event. Rejected: the caller passing it to the exporter, which fails silently when omitted. (2) A model client may declare an optional read-only provider_name, read once per run as default_model_id is (FR-32); ModelCalled records it as provider_name, None when undeclared, and gen_ai.provider.name is set from it. OpenAICompatibleModelClient declares none, because the gateway fronts several providers. Rejected: a mapping given to the exporter, and leaving the attribute out of M14. SPEC FR-57, FR-58, FR-59, AC-45 and AC-46 amended.

decisions.title: M14 round 1: C1 and C2 are fixed before M14 is completed, with a round 2 review of that change
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-15 after the M14 round 1 review. C2 is treated as a defect rather than a caveat: a before_model hook naming the model as a StrEnum member or a str subclass made ModelCalled.model record the run model (priced) while the client received the named model (other) and the call was priced as it (cost 2.000 beside model priced), against AC-45, reproduced by the owner and in memory by the implementing session. Cause: loop.py _sent_model accepts only an exact str while the Runner cost_of prices any str. C1 is fixed with it although FR-48 already calls a cross-loop export misuse. Both fixes are written test first, the mutation run covers the changed code, both gates are rerun, and a round 2 review covers only this change. C3 to C9 stay recorded caveats. M14 is not completed until round 2 approves.

decisions.title: M14 completed after round 2, with R1 as a follow-up
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-15: M14 is completed on the round 2 approval without a round 3, because R1 needs a reader on another thread event loop, which FR-48 already excludes, the exporter follows on the run loop, and no run was affected in any trial. Follow-up, before any later milestone relies on readers on other loops: in handle.py _stream, check _ended and the next event again after appending the waiter; add a Postgres version of the cross-loop iterator test; add tests for a str subclass overriding __str__ or __len__ as a model name, for the done check in _resolve, for flush with several followed handles, and for a stopped but unclosed run loop; and correct the _wake docstring, which overstates cross-loop safety. R2 stays a recorded caveat. The commit is not published to GitHub (owner decision).

decisions.title: M15: the Claude Code CLI is installed locally under evals/adr12 and pinned
decisions.text: Owner decision 2026-09-16 at the M15 pre-flight. The Claude Agent SDK spawns the Claude Code CLI, which was not installed on this machine. The CLI is installed under evals/adr12 with npm, pinned to 2.1.267 in evals/adr12/package.json and its lock file, and the harness points the SDK at evals/adr12/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe through ClaudeAgentOptions cli_path. Nothing is installed machine-wide, so a later global upgrade cannot change the comparison, and the pinned version is named in the report (FR-62). evals/adr12/node_modules is gitignored, while evals/adr12/reports stays visible so that the credential scan reads the report (AC-50). Rejected: a global npm install, which changes the machine and moves with any later upgrade.

decisions.title: M15 round 1 follow-ups carried into the next increment
decisions.text: Three items from the M15 round 1 review are carried forward rather than fixed in M15, on the owner decision of 2026-09-16. None of them affects the delivered 72 row report, which was checked row by row. F1: the retries-from-settings and entry-count checkers in evals/adr12/tasks.py match their wanted digit as a bare substring, so an answer of 15 retries or 16 entries would pass although the fixture says 5 retries and 6 entries. Match the number as a whole word instead, before the comparison is ever run again, because a future run could otherwise record a wrong pass. F2: when a Claude arm run fails before its result message arrives, RunOutcome reports turns and every token count as zero and the cost as zero, which reads as a measured zero rather than the unavailable sentinel that the same row already uses for the SDK cost estimate. Return unavailable on that path so a failed row cannot be read as a cheap one. F3: equalise the two arm prompts or record both of them in the report metadata and pin both in the gate, per KNOWLEDGE-66f5b06a, and treat the token gap as unexplained per KNOWLEDGE-eba388f8. F1 and F2 both touch hashed files, so they arrive with their own gate run and their own independent review; they are not covered by the M15 approval. The M15 review also left two gaps of its own, recorded here so the next reviewer can close them: only 2 of the 20 author mutants were rerun and no new mutant was invented, and the removed CLI probe was substituted with a static check plus proxy poisoning because a rename was blocked by the sandbox.

decisions.title: Phase 2 increment 2: plan, criteria, loops, replanning, result contract and run scope (P2-D15 to P2-D18, P2-D22, P2-D26)
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-09-16, before any increment 2 requirement was written. P2-D15: the planner emits a JSON document validated against a shipped schema and stored as an immutable PlanVersion with parent_plan, with a RunStateStore holding node status. Taken as settled rather than put to the owner, because ADR-03 already requires immutable versions with parent_plan and the design calls the plan a persisted and visible object; an in memory plan cannot answer why a run did what it did after the fact. P2-D16: the acceptance criteria increment 2 can actually check are deterministic only, namely that output validates against expected_output_schema, that a named artifact exists with a recorded checksum, and that a named tool returns success. A critic typed criterion parses but is refused at runtime until Phase 3 builds the critic, which keeps Phase 3 additive and keeps a plan written now valid then. P2-D17: no loop nodes. Convergence goes through replanning bounded by max_replans, so ADR-02 stays DAG-only; the cost is one plan version per round and the gain is that every round is audited. Reopening ADR-02 remains scheduled for Phase 5A. Closes backlog I-01. P2-D18: replanning proceeds automatically while budget remains and the replan count is under its limit, and never reruns a completed side effecting node. PlanNode gains a side_effecting flag defaulting to True, so the unsafe case is the default. P2-D22: a subagent result that fails its output schema is re-asked once with the validation error appended, then the node fails with output_contract_violation. The retry draws on that node own reservation, so it cannot escape the budget. P2-D26: a tool reaches its run through an explicit RunScope argument passed to the tool callable, not through a context variable, because M11 and M12 showed how much grief implicit cross loop context causes and an explicit argument is what a test can pin.

decisions.title: Phase 2 increment 2: the ADR-06 budget numbers and a pricing source (P2-D19, P2-D20)
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-09-16. P2-D19 fills the four figures DECISION-e1bf0327 left to this specification and closes backlog I-05. A planner proposed budget_reservation is capped at 40 percent of the currently unallocated pool, so no single node can starve its siblings. Nodes for which the planner proposes no reservation split the unallocated pool equally. The orchestrator reserve is 20 percent of the run ceiling and the unallocated reserve is another 20 percent, and the unallocated reserve is the only source of additional allocation, drawn by deterministic orchestrator policy and never at the request of a model. All four are fields on BudgetPolicy and these are their defaults, so a run works out of the box and a deployment can tighten them. P2-D20 closes backlog I-13: a price table with an explicit date ships inside the package, a caller supplied ModelPricing overrides it, and a USD budget on a model absent from the table is a configuration error raised at the call site rather than a silently unpriced call. The date is part of the table and is reported, so a stale price cannot be read as current fact. Token ceilings continue to work for every model with or without a price. Rejected: requiring every caller to supply prices, which is how cost_usd came to be None today and would make USD budgets unusable out of the box; and fetching prices at runtime, which this gateway does not allow because /model/info returns 403.

decisions.title: Phase 2 increment 2: limits, tool visibility, compaction, deferrals and the milestone split (P2-D21, P2-D23, P2-D24, P2-D25, P2-D27)
decisions.text: Owner accepted on 2026-09-16. P2-D21: recursion depth 3, which is orchestrator then child then grandchild, raising MaxDepthExceeded beyond it; max_concurrent_subagents 4; max_tasks_per_run 50; queue_policy FIFO. Depth 3 allows hub and spoke with one nesting, and 4 concurrent bounds the budget overshoot that soft enforcement permits to four model calls. P2-D23 reverses DECISION-ca1ad3e0 for subagents and closes backlog I-14: an agent is sent only the schemas of the tools its profile lets it execute, so visibility follows execution. The argument is mechanism rather than the M15 gap, whose cause is unmeasured per KNOWLEDGE-eba388f8: every unusable schema is prompt tokens on every turn of every child, and a tool that is visible but not callable invites a wasted turn. The consequence is recorded deliberately: the tool set an agent actually saw becomes part of what the ExecutionManifest must record, or two runs sharing a manifest could have seen different tools. P2-D24 closes backlog I-17 and I-24: ContextCompactor triggers at a configurable fraction of the model context window, default 0.75; the summary inherits the maximum taint of everything it summarises and keeps provenance for every source it names; and each compaction is recorded as an artifact and a run event, so a compacted run can still be audited. Caller triggered compaction was rejected because an unattended long run is exactly the failure that moved compaction forward from Phase 7. P2-D25 defers two outline items: sibling stagger for prompt cache reuse, backlog I-02, waits for the native Anthropic adapter because the OpenAI compatible gateway exposes no cache control markers and there is nothing to stagger for yet; and scanning child output for instruction shaped text, backlog I-03, waits for Phase 4, because taint labels already stop a tainted result from triggering an action and scanning is defence in depth rather than the missing control. P2-D27 splits increment 2 into five milestones, smallest provable step first: M16 PlanVersion and RunStateStore, the plan as a persisted immutable object across both stores; M17 the budget governor with reservations, reclaim, soft enforcement and the dated price table; M18 subagents with curated briefing, hub and spoke, the structured result contract, the depth limit and SchedulerLimits; M19 the orchestrator itself, DAG execution over the plan, acceptance criteria and replanning; M20 ContextPolicy and ContextCompactor. Every milestone keeps one exact demo command that proves it works.

decisions.title: M16 clarifications of FR-64 and FR-66: node events and forward node fields
decisions.text: Owner decided on 2026-09-19 during the M16 pre-flight, which found two places where the approved specification did not say enough to build M16. First, FR-66 says node transitions appear in the run event stream, but the event sink is per run and owns sequence numbering, and nothing runs nodes until the M19 orchestrator; AC-51 and AC-52 test no events. Decided: M16 adds the event types PlanNodeStarted and PlanNodeFinished and one transition path that writes the node status row and emits the event through that run own sink, with the node id in the envelope task_id column that the schema already reserves for Phase 2 and plan_id and version in the payload. M16 tests prove the row and the event together on both stores with sequence_no contiguous; seeing them live through RunHandle.events is proven by AC-58 in M19, once the orchestrator drives nodes. Rejected: moving the events to M19, which would split FR-66 across two milestones and risk reshaping the M16 store API. Second, FR-64 gives PlanNode an acceptance_criteria field whose behaviour is FR-74 in M19 and a budget_reservation field whose behaviour is FR-67 in M17, while AC-51 requires a field for field round trip and P2-D16 requires a plan written now to stay valid later. Decided: M16 fixes both stored shapes with no behaviour. AcceptanceCriterion carries its four kinds, output_schema, artifact_exists, tool_succeeds and critic, with their fields; a reservation carries an optional USD Decimal and an optional token count. M19 adds evaluation and M17 adds enforcement without changing either stored shape. Rejected: opaque JSON until then, which could leave a plan stored in M16 invalid against the later types.

decisions.title: M16 round 1: F3 blocks completion; F1 and F5 fixed with it; F2 and F4 carried to M19
decisions.text: The M16 round 1 reviewer, Fable 5.1, approved with caveats F1 to F5. The owner verified F1 to F3 first-hand and argued that F3 breaks AC-51, leaving the call to the implementing session, which decided on 2026-09-19 that F3 blocks. AC-51 requires a plan on both stores to read back field for field with its plan_hash unchanged; on Postgres, floats that JSON writes in exponent form such as 1e16 and 1e300, and negative zero, inside expected_output_schema or criterion arguments came back normalised by JSONB with a different hash, from valid planner input and silently, while the in-memory store kept them. The author had already fixed A6, the same class of defect, as a defect. F3 also covers get_plan never comparing the recomputed hash with the stored one, so a document edited in the database read back without error. Fix: the document is stored as its exact canonical text rather than JSONB, and get_plan refuses a row whose recomputed hash differs from its stored hash. F1, fixed in the same pass: plan_id was a global key, so another tenant could store a version under an existing plan_id, blocking the owner replan, and learn from the refusal that the plan exists; plan identity becomes tenant, project, plan_id and version on both stores. F5, fixed in the same pass because it breaks the pinned contract that every refusal raises InvalidPlan: nesting 200 or 800 deep raised RecursionError; depth is bounded and refused as InvalidPlan. Both fixes change migration 0007, which was never committed or released but was applied to the development database; the owner chose to rewrite 0007 in place and reset its two tables on the development database, holding only 14 example-tenant demo rows, rather than add a migration and renumber the specification. Carried to M19, before anything drives nodes: F2, a transition accepts any event sink, so a node event can land in another run; F4, on Postgres the row lock ends at commit before the emit, so two racing transitions of one node can record Finished before Started. A7 stands as declared, judged by the reviewer not a breach of NFR-22 as written. A round 2 review runs on a different model after the fixes.

knowledge.title: Gateway fronts 308 models across four providers
knowledge.text: GET /models (not /v1/models, which Envoy blocks with 'fault filter abort' 403) lists 308 model ids namespaced by provider: bedrock.*, azure.*, openai.*, vertex_ai.*. Tool calling verified working on both openai.gpt-4o-mini and bedrock.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5 through the identical OpenAI-shaped request, so provider switching in Phase 0 is a model-id change rather than an adapter change.

knowledge.title: Genesis gate commands must use Windows path separators
knowledge.text: genesis.mjs executes gate commands through cmd.exe on win32. A command beginning with a forward-slash path such as .venv/Scripts/python.exe fails with "'.venv' is not recognized" because cmd parses /Scripts as a switch. Gate commands on this host must be written .venv\Scripts\python.exe. The CLI has no gate-edit path (task add rejects duplicate ids, task set ignores --gate), so correcting a gate means editing .genesis/project.json directly; that is safe because validateState checks only schema_version and policy, and gate evidence hashes are recomputed on each run.

knowledge.title: genesis checkpoint and index crash on this host via the Store Python alias
knowledge.text: graphizer.mjs spawns python3 to build the Python AST, then spawns git for the revision. On this machine python3 and python both resolve to the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias, which corrupts the Node process job-object state; the following git spawn dies natively with AssignProcessToJobObject (87), exit 3 / 0xC0000003. Minimal repro: spawnSync(python3, {input}) followed by spawnSync(git) in one Node process. Verified the real .venv/Scripts/python.exe does NOT trigger it, so the alias is the cause, and the base interpreter under C:/Program Files/WindowsApps is not directly executable. Consequence: genesis checkpoint, genesis index and genesis kickoff fail; gate, task, record, spec, plan and status all work. Fix is to disable the python.exe/python3.exe app execution aliases in Windows Settings, or install python.org Python. Not a blocker for building.

knowledge.title: Store Python alias crash is fixed by the venv, no Windows settings change needed
knowledge.text: Resolves the earlier AssignProcessToJobObject finding. A Windows venv ships python.exe and pythonw.exe but no python3.exe, so graphizer's spawnSync('python3') fell through to the Microsoft Store app execution alias. Copying .venv/Scripts/python.exe to .venv/Scripts/python3.exe and putting that directory first on PATH makes python3 resolve to the real interpreter; genesis checkpoint then succeeds and indexes 159 nodes with no warnings. Run genesis as: PATH="$PWD/.venv/Scripts:$PATH" node <kit>/tools/genesis.mjs <cmd> . -- or just activate the venv first. NOTE: .venv is gitignored, so python3.exe must be recreated after any fresh venv build; see requirements.txt header.

knowledge.title: Redaction must precede truncation, and dict.get needs a hashable key
knowledge.text: Two boundary bugs found in round 2 of L4 review, both in code written to fix round 1. (1) _error_text truncated a provider body to 300 chars and then replaced the credential, so a key straddling the cut survived as a recoverable 14-character fragment in a ModelError message that FR-10 persists. Redact the whole text first, truncate second. (2) _STOP_REASONS.get(choice.get('finish_reason')) assumed the value was hashable; a list or dict finish_reason raised TypeError: unhashable type, escaping the adapter and violating the invariant that only AgentSDKError subclasses leave ModelClient.send(). Using an unchecked value as a dict key is itself a shape assumption.

knowledge.title: Reviewer rotation found defects that reviewer effort did not
knowledge.text: M3 took five review rounds. Rounds 1-3 were one reviewer, which found exactly one boundary escape per round, all in the same region (the response parse path), each fix enumerating one more exception type. Round 4 swapped models and immediately found an escape in a region the first reviewer never examined: the totaliser's own error-message construction, where str(exc) runs inside the except block. Round 5, a third model running 20 hostile boundary probes and 39 mutants, found no escape at all. Conclusion for the remaining milestones: rotate the reviewer model between rounds rather than asking the same reviewer to look harder. A reviewer cannot find the defects its own mental model does not generate, and repeated rounds from one reviewer converge on its blind spots rather than on correctness.

knowledge.title: M5 must redact the chained __cause__ and traceback, not only the ModelError message
knowledge.text: Five rounds of redaction work covered the ModelError message text only. The adapter raises 'from exc', so the original provider exception is retained on __cause__ with its message unredacted, and the traceback holds frame locals. When M5 serialises RunEvent payloads (FR-10) or writes a RunFailed row, anything that walks __cause__, __context__ or formats a traceback bypasses every redaction built so far. This must be a stated requirement of the persistence layer, not a discovery in M5's review: the event writer redacts what it serialises, or it must refuse to serialise exception chains at all.

knowledge.title: Gate gaps hide as quality degradation, not failure
knowledge.text: The most valuable finding of M4's second review was not a defect but a gate gap: an assembler that forwarded only the last message survived all 222 tests. The existing tests checked that a tool message EXISTED in the request, and the assembler unit test used a single-message history, so nothing pinned full-history assembly. A run with truncated context does not fail -- it silently gets worse, which is the hardest failure mode to notice. Verified the gap by mutating the assembler (222 passed), added tests for full-history assembly and growing per-turn history, and re-verified the mutation is now caught (2 failures). Same treatment applied to RuntimeHook HALT and MODIFY at all four points, which were likewise unpinned. General lesson: when reviewing a gate, ask which mutations would degrade quality rather than break behaviour -- those are the ones tests forget.

knowledge.title: Concurrent appends are safe but not available; Phase 2 needs a retry or lock
knowledge.text: Measured, not assumed. PostgresSessionStore.append uses INSERT ... SELECT COALESCE(MAX(sequence_no),0)+1 inside one transaction. Under READ COMMITTED two concurrent transactions can read the same MAX. Probed with 12 barrier-synchronised writers on one run: 8 rows committed with unique contiguous sequence numbers 1..8, 0 duplicates, and 4 writers raised UniqueViolation. So SAFETY holds absolutely (no duplicate or reordered history can commit, guaranteed by UNIQUE (run_id, sequence_no)) while AVAILABILITY does not (a losing writer errors rather than serialising). Phase 0 has exactly one writer per run so this is unreachable today. Phase 2's concurrent subagents will need a retry-on-UniqueViolation loop or a per-run advisory lock; the safety property is pinned by a test so a future fix cannot regress it.

knowledge.title: Database tests can prove the database, not the code
knowledge.text: Against a real database a passing test often proves the DATABASE behaves rather than that the CODE is right. Two instances in M5: (1) CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS means mutating schema.sql cannot affect an already-created database, so schema assertions proved the live DB, not the file; (2) removing ORDER BY sequence_no survived every test because an append-only table returns rows in insertion order anyway. The fix in both cases is to make the environment stop cooperating: apply the schema into a throwaway namespace, and write rows out of order before asserting a read is ordered. Both were found by mutation, not by reading.

knowledge.title: Concurrent append: safety fixed, availability varies
knowledge.text: Re-measured after tenancy derivation changed the insert to a LEFT JOIN with GROUP BY. Three 12-writer trials: 0 duplicates and contiguous sequence numbers every time (safety unchanged), with 1, 1 and 0 UniqueViolation losers respectively -- previously a steady 4 of 12. Availability is timing-dependent and the failure mode is still reachable, so the Phase 2 retry-or-advisory-lock item stands; the earlier '4 of 12' figure should not be quoted as a fixed property.

knowledge.title: Name what you can, then back it with a total check
knowledge.text: unstorable_reason has two layers: named checks (NUL, non-finite, depth) for a precise diagnosis, and a backstop that attempts the serialisation the store actually performs -- json.dumps(allow_nan=False, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8'). Round 3 shipped only the named layer and round 4 found a lone UTF-16 surrogate walking past it: a truncated surrogate escape is a legal RFC-8259 decode, models emit truncated pairs, and both TEXT and JSONB refuse the result. The backstop catches the CLASS (anything the serialiser cannot express) rather than the instance, which also closed huge integers for free. Same structure as the ModelClient total boundary: specific guards for good messages, one total guard for correctness. Verified in BOTH directions against a live database -- astral emoji, 4-byte CJK and int(1e308) are still accepted, so the helper does not over-reject and fail runs that should work.

knowledge.title: Name a test after the invariant it pins
knowledge.text: A round-4 reviewer reported INVARIANT-3c123c38 (token_count must not swallow BaseException) as unpinned, having mutated it and seen the usage-related subset stay green. The mutation does turn the FULL suite red -- the test existed -- but it was named test_base_exception_from_a_hostile_int_still_propagates, so no 'pytest -k usage' or '-k token_count' selection could find it. Renamed to test_usage_token_count_lets_base_exception_propagate; all three selections now go red. A guard nobody can locate is one a reviewer reasonably concludes is missing, and reviewers work by subset selection.

knowledge.title: Over-rejection is a defect in the same class as under-rejection
knowledge.text: unstorable_reason capped nesting at depth 60 and called anything deeper unstorable. Postgres stores 900-deep JSON without complaint, so a model returning deeply nested tool arguments had its call refused over a limit that does not exist. Found by probing the database for the helper's false positives, not by review -- four review rounds had all hunted the other direction. Fix: the walk is iterative with a visited-id set instead of recursive with a depth cap, so it never guesses about depth; the serialiser decides, and it happens to agree with Postgres exactly (both stop at ~1000, the interpreter recursion limit). Walking iteratively also keeps the named checks looking at any depth: deferring on depth would have stopped finding a NUL buried 300 levels down, which the backstop cannot catch because JSON escapes NUL happily.

knowledge.title: Overlapping guards need a test at each layer
knowledge.text: Two mutations survived the round-6 matrix because the storability guards overlap: removing ModelResponse's field walk still passed end-to-end, since _json_safe marks the same value downstream, and vice versa. Overlap is deliberate defence in depth, but an end-to-end test cannot pin either layer -- it only proves that at least one still works. Each layer now has a test at its own level (ModelResponse asserted directly on the type; _json_safe asserted on both its string and its str()-fallback branch). Where a mutation survives because another layer covers it, the answer is a narrower test, not a weaker claim.

knowledge.title: An exemption in the test is the tell
knowledge.text: Round 6 found ToolCall.__post_init__ exempting arguments_error from the field walk introduced in round 5 to end exemptions -- and the test asserting 'the guarantee is structural, not a list of names' contained 'if name == arguments_error: continue'. The fix and its guard were written together and the guard was shaped around the gap, so the suite could never have caught it. When a test carries a special case for the code under test, treat the special case as the finding, not as scaffolding: verify the exemption is load-bearing by deleting it and running the suite. Here it was not -- 380 tests passed with it gone.

knowledge.title: Two guards for one property hide each other
knowledge.text: Second occurrence in two rounds. The round-6 fix added BOTH a field-walk covering arguments_error and a follow-up check on the generated reason string; reintroducing the carve-out then left all 380 tests green, because whichever guard was removed the other still produced a storable value. The second guard was also unreachable -- the reason string is built from field names and our own messages, always ASCII. Resolution: keep the structural guard, delete the unreachable one. Where two guards enforce the SAME property rather than different ones, the redundancy does not add defence; it removes the suite's ability to notice either one being deleted. Compare KNOWLEDGE-fd4720a4, where the layers guarded genuinely different surfaces and the answer was a test per layer.

knowledge.title: Implementing a caveat's list is not implementing the caveat
knowledge.text: Round 6's caveat (c) read 'tenant_id, project_id, agent_spec_id and model_id are unchecked for storability'. The repair implemented exactly those four names, and round 7 rejected on principal_context -- the fifth caller-supplied value, which the caveat had not enumerated. A review names examples; the finding is the class. Read every caveat as 'what is the property, and where else does it fail?' rather than as a checklist. Same failure mode as rounds 5 and 6 (a check applied to the fields someone thought of), arriving this time through the review process itself rather than through the code.

knowledge.title: Test that a guard is RIGHT, not that it runs
knowledge.text: Rounds 5-7 were all 'the guard was not applied to X'. Round 8 was different and worse: the guard was applied, named, and tested -- and answered the wrong question. max_turns was validated with unstorable_reason, a JSON serialisability predicate, while runs.max_turns is INTEGER, so 2**31 passed the guard and failed at the write. The round-7 test asserted only that each parameter name appeared in a set of checked names, which a check returning the wrong answer passes trivially. Removing the max_turns check entirely left all 389 tests green. Coverage tests answer 'does a check run'; fitness tests answer 'does it refuse what the column refuses'. Only the second kind can fail. The replacement drives a genuinely unfit value through every parameter and requires a refusal.

knowledge.title: A carve-out copied between layers loses its reason
knowledge.text: column_rejection_reason excluded bools from the INTEGER range check with . That exclusion was copied from token_count, where it is right (a flag is not a token count) -- but in a column check its effect is the opposite: psycopg adapts a bool to SQL boolean, so True reaches an integer column as DatatypeMismatch after completing happily in memory. The exclusion looked harmless because True is trivially inside the int32 range, which is answering a different question again. When moving a guard between layers, re-derive why each exception exists rather than carrying it across.

knowledge.title: A mutation that proves a leak test must not write the real secret
knowledge.text: While mutation-testing M6's AC-10 assertion I mutated api.py to copy MODEL_API_KEY into runs.agent_spec_id. It worked -- the test caught it -- but the five rows outlived the mutation by the length of the restore, so a real credential sat in the database until the next gate run found it. Remediated by redacting the column in place (pinned to the key pattern, the test tenants and today's date), verified zero rows anywhere afterwards. The mutation now writes LEAK-CANARY-<first four chars>, which proves the value came from the key without the row ever holding it, and the AC-10 test scans for the canary as well so the mutation is still detectable. The harness also clears its own canary rows, because debris that fails a credential gate looks exactly like a real leak to whoever runs it next. General rule: a destructive mutation must be as reversible as the restore that follows it.

knowledge.title: Live models cannot be prompted into a validation failure
knowledge.text: AC-3 needs a malformed tool argument. Asked to call echo with the number 42, openai.gpt-4o-mini sends 42 and trips ToolValidationError, while bedrock.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5 coerces it to the string 42 and validates cleanly -- measured twice per provider. Providers increasingly enforce the declared schema server-side, so a malformed argument from a compliant provider is rare, which is exactly why the SDK's validate step exists as defence rather than as a formality. Consequence for the golden eval: AC-1 and AC-2 are asserted on the live path (both providers reliably call the denied tool when instructed), AC-3 is asserted on a scripted run where the malformed call is guaranteed. An assertion that depends on which model happens to be strict is a flaky gate.

knowledge.title: Measure the class, not the one shape you tried
knowledge.text: M6 round 1 was rejected for not exercising AC-3 live, and my justification was that a validation failure cannot be driven by prompting -- measured twice per provider. The measurement was real but it covered ONE shape: a number where a string is declared, which openai rejects and claude coerces. The reviewer tested a different shape, a maxLength 8 constraint the instructed input cannot satisfy, and got ToolValidationError on both providers 4 runs out of 4 with the implementation never invoked. Reproduced here before believing it. A measurement justifying a design decision must cover the CLASS the decision is about, and the decision should name which shapes were tried. Same error as the guard defects in M5: generalising from the instance in front of me.

knowledge.title: Assert the property the criterion names, not something adjacent
knowledge.text: The M6 reviewer found four tests, all passing, each asserting one step removed from its claim: AC-10 said 'no credential in any row' but scanned an enumerated column subset (it missed a canary in run_events.tool_call_id on 120 rows); AC-2 said 'surfaced to the model' but read the persisted history; NFR-4 said 'no credential in model context' but inspected the ModelRequest object rather than the wire body; NFR-7 said principal_context is never read but asserted an error type rather than the decision. In every case the SDK was correct, so these were gate defects -- tests passing for reasons weaker than the claims they underwrite. Fixes: whole-row scans over every table via {table}::text, assertions on the next request actually sent, a recording httpx transport for the wire body, and identical decisions across three different principals. When writing a test, say the criterion out loud and check the assertion is about that noun.

knowledge.title: Mutation debris makes later mutations look killed
knowledge.text: Re-running the M6 matrix, the first mutation wrote a canary into run_events.tool_call_id. My cleanup script only knew about runs.agent_spec_id, so 162 rows survived -- and then failed the AC-10 test on every SUBSEQUENT mutation, making all of them look killed by it. The matrix was worthless in a way that reads as success.
